messages:
maria_ng: heads-up — want to capture quick notes from yesterday's pairing on a compact coalescer + slot smoothing approach. thinking about the long-tail latency tradeoffs we hit in prod
samir: +1. saw the tail spikes when tenant A bursts for ~200 requests in 2s. current coalesce window shrinks throughput too much if we bias for latency
jin_park: main trade I keep circling: smaller windows -> better p50/p95 but loses batching efficiency and increases GPU kernel churn. larger windows -> cost down, tail up
alex_r: real-world ask: keep interactive latency under 150ms for tier-1 routes while not dropping unit-economics by 20%. can we do adaptive windows per-tenant?
maria_ng: proposal sketch: two-layer admission: lightweight fastpath for tiny requests (<128 tokens) that bypasses long coalesce; otherwise go to compact coalesce with smoothing credits
samir: how do we avoid starvation? if fastpath floods, compact coalesce never gets enough tokens to form efficient batches
jin_park: add a credit drain limiter: every N fastpath ops we allow one compact batch to drain, plus a soft-eviction hysteresis for long-running tenants
alex_r: needs clear metrics. can we export headroom_gauge, drain_rate, fastpath_ratio at route/token granularity? ops wants alerting on fastpath_ratio > 0.8 for 30s
maria_ng: agreed. telemetry also needs to expose "coalesce_fill" histogram and "compact_evicts" counter. those let us tune hysteresis
samir: what about KV cache interaction? compact coalesce delays might evict useful KV entries. we should tie headroom to KV reuse score
jin_park: rough API: attach "cache_importance" score to requests. scheduler uses score to bump priority when deciding to flush a compact batch
alex_r: can we see a small config example?
maria_ng: sample config we discussed:
```
coalesce:
  min_window_ms: 2
  max_window_ms: 40
  smoothing_alpha: 0.2
  fastpath_quota: 100/s
  compact_drain_every: 20
  eviction_hysteresis_ms: 200
```

samir: seems reasonable. one caution: smoothing_alpha interacts badly with bursty diurnal patterns; we should cap window adjustments per-second to avoid oscillation
jin_park: implement a step limiter and add a cooldown per-tenant after a canary resize. that'll reduce thrash
alex_r: rollout plan: A/B on a small fleet with synthetic bursts, look at p99, cost/tokens, and KV hit-rate. ops will stage alerts for regressions
maria_ng: follow-ups: I'll open a short RFC with the config knobs + metrics & rollout checklist. tagging @deploy-bot to kick off perf tests
deploy-bot: perf-test queued: compact-coalesce-smoke, 4 runs, region-us-west-2. results ETA: 202s
